notes:
ATTEMPT 3. Both MAJOR findings from attempt 2 are resolved.

The important one was a visible buttonhole stitched onto the outer face of a collar leaf. This option is HIDDEN BUTTON: the button sits under the leaf and its buttonhole is cut on the shirt front beneath, so from outside the collar reads completely clean. A visible buttonhole does not merely differ from the drawing — it renders the option as its own opposite, and makes it indistinguishable from the sibling option that sells a visible button-down. Both leaves are now plain and unbroken.

The second major was an angled three-quarter viewpoint that left the two leaves visibly unequal, one folded and foreshortened. The square frontal view the drawing itself uses fixed it, exactly as it did for collar-point-70 — the same lesson twice, and worth stating plainly: when a drawing is orthographic and symmetric, photographing it from an angle costs symmetry every time.

What made the correction land was naming what the construction MEANS rather than only what to omit: 'the button is sewn on the UNDERSIDE of the leaf, with its buttonhole on the shirt front beneath; from outside the collar looks completely clean.' The same shape of fix as the red-annotation clause — describe the thing, not just the prohibition.

All nine categories at or above 95 with zero Critical or Major findings, so this qualifies for the logged waiver at attempt 3.
